boundaries.evidence: Empty fibres have zero cohomology. Step 4.1 treats empty and zero-dimensional fibre components directly; step 7.1 treats disconnected bases componentwise and the empty base vacuously.
Step 3.1 identifies the zero cohomology groups and their zero lattices; step 4.1 gives type (0,0) in degree zero and zero other types on zero-dimensional fibres.
The continuous harmonic-kernel argument of step 4.1 and the polarization of step 5.1 include rank-one pieces.
Step 4.1 treats fibre components separately when their dimensions differ. Steps 6.1–7.1 handle tensor, dual and summand closures and extend lattices and polarizations from the realization open.
Step 2.1 proves whole-path horizontal continuation from compactness and relative smoothing, and step 3.1 constructs the full-fibre radial trivialization.

AC supplies partitions and Whitney approximation, analytic Hodge inputs, abelian injective resolutions and the local cochain/refinement assignments in step 1.2, and free integer boundary bases in its contractibility argument. These uses are explicit in F9–F11 and steps 2.1–4.1.

boundaries.reason: The statement is a list of existence and closure assertions, not a biconditional.
No converse direction is asserted.

template_review.reason: Statement constructs local systems, full integral lattices and polarizations from smooth projective families and proves geometric closure operations. A polarized rational variation with a lattice is not asserted to arise from such a family.

risk_review.notes: Read all eight steps and every cited dependency interface. Checked analytic properness via closed projective embedding and compact sphere/product, compact horizontal-ODE continuation and inverse-pullback covariance, Z-valued flasque singular-cochain resolution with free contractible small-chain quotient and supplied injective dimension shifting, finite-CW lattice comparison modulo torsion, continuous harmonic kernels via invertible Delta+Pi and constant Betti number, type idempotents and zero-dimensional/empty fibres. Flat relative Chern class gives rational polarized Lefschetz decomposition; rational Kunneth avoids integral torsion assumptions. Rational tensor/summand lattices are obtained by intersection; Tate twists and duals have the correct signs and finite sum realizations. Surjective open fundamental groups extend lattices/forms; density and continuous nondegenerate Hermitian eigenvalues extend positivity. AC covers all infinite basis/cover/resolution inputs. Sources Deligne II 4.2.1-4.2.5 were read in full; no unresolved risk.

citations.quote:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a geometric polarizable rational
Hodge variation ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]) on a connected
smooth quasiprojective complex variety $S$. For each base point $s$, the
monodromy-invariant space $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$
([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is a Hodge substructure of
$H_s$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), and parallel transport
identifies these spaces as one constant Hodge structure. Equivalently, the Hodge
components of every global flat section are global flat sections. For
$H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with $f:X\to S$ smooth projective and an SNC smooth
projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$, the image of
$H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is exactly the invariant
space.

Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional
rational algebra. The socle ([[def-socle-of-a-module]]) of the
$A_{\mathbb C}$-module $V_{\mathbb C}$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$: it is
$W\otimes\mathbb C$ for a rational $A$-submodule $W\subseteq V$. If $V\ne0$,
then $W\ne0$.

For a left $R$-module $M$, the **socle** is $$\operatorname{Soc}(M):=\sum\{S\le M:S\text{ is simple}\}.$$ Concretely it is the submodule generated by the union of all simple submodules. If there are none, the sum is $0$, so the definition is always meaningful.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a smooth projective morphism
$f:X\to S$ of smooth quasiprojective complex varieties, $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a
finite-rank local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]),
with full monodromy-stable integral lattice obtained from
$R^mf_*\mathbb Z$ modulo torsion, and with a continuous pure Hodge
decomposition of weight $m$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]). A
relatively ample line bundle supplies flat Lefschetz operators and a flat
rational polarization of this variation. Products, sums, Tate twists, exterior
powers and Hodge direct summands have the corresponding geometric realizations
and full integral lattices. Pullbacks of algebraic maps between smooth
projective fibers preserve rational Hodge structures.

For a finite-length module, the direct-sum, sum-of-simples, and complement characterizations of semisimplicity are equivalent without any choice principle. See [[thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-semisimple-modules]].
A left $R$-module is **semisimple** when it is an internal direct sum of simple submodules, allowing the empty direct sum. Hence the zero module is semisimple.

Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$ and let $\bigl(x^{(j)}\bigr)_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$
be a sequence in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ whose range
$\{\, x^{(j)} : j \in \mathbb{N} \,\}$ is a bounded subset of
$(\mathbb{R}^{n}, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]], [[lem-metrics-on-rn]]).
Then there are a strictly increasing $i : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
([[def-sequence]], [[lem-index-map-grows]]) and a point $p \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$
with

$$x^{(i_j)} \longrightarrow p \quad \text{in } (\mathbb{R}^{n}, d_2)$$

([[def-metric-convergence]]). By [[thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent]] the same
statement holds with $d_2$ replaced by the metric of any norm on
$\mathbb{R}^{n}$, boundedness and convergence both being unchanged by that
replacement ([[def-equivalent-norms]]).

**This is assembled from published theorems and is not proved again by
bisection.** The bisection is in [[thm-heine-borel-rn]], published at order 120;
what is added here is the passage from compactness to sequential compactness and
the reading of the conclusion in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$.

**Choice cost: none.** [[thm-heine-borel-rn]] is proved by bisection and uses no
choice principle, and "compact implies sequentially compact" is a theorem of ZF
([[thm-compact-implies-the-other-compactness-forms]]). The five-way equivalence
[[thm-metric-compactness-equivalences]] is **not** used, precisely because it is
stated under countable choice and dependent choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]) and
would overcharge this corollary; the arrow-by-arrow account is
[[rem-compactness-choice-ledger-metric]].

Let $S$ be connected and let $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}$ be a finite-rank rational
local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). If
$\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple, then
$\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes k$ is semisimple for every characteristic-zero
field $k$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]). In particular this applies to rational
Gauss-Manin local systems after complex geometric semisimplicity has been
proved. The field $k$ need not embed in $\mathbb C$. Semisimplicity means that
every monodromy-invariant subspace has an invariant complement, equivalently
that the monodromy module is a finite direct sum of simple modules.

derivations.claim: Rational descent of the socle and its lattice. Let $H$ be a nonzero pure geometric object of rank $r$ over the connected base $S$, and let $W_{\mathbb C}$ be the socle of the complex monodromy module $V_{s,\mathbb C}$, a nonzero finite-dimensional complex module by [F2]. By [F2] there is a rational flat subspace $W_{\mathbb Q}\subseteq V_s$ with $W_{\mathbb C}=W_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$; since it is monodromy-invariant it is the fibre at $s$ of a local subsystem of $H$, which we again call $W$. Let $H_{\mathbb Z}$ be the full monodromy-stable integral lattice of [F3] and put $W_{\mathbb Z}=W_{\mathbb Q}\cap H_{\mathbb Z}$; a rational basis of $W_{\mathbb Q}$ becomes integral after clearing denominators, so $W_{\mathbb Z}$ is a full lattice in $W_{\mathbb Q}$, and the monodromy preserves it and acts by invertible integral matrices. On the determinant line $\det W=\bigwedge^{e}W$, $e=\dim_{\mathbb Q}W_{\mathbb Q}$, the monodromy therefore acts by $\pm1$, so $(\det W)^{\otimes2}$ is a constant rank-one local subsystem of the geometric tensor object $\bigwedge^eH\otimes\bigwedge^eH$ of [F3], generated by a global horizontal section.

Torus images of simple summands are flat. Write the complex socle as $W_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_i S_i$ by [F4]. Fix a summand $T$ of dimension $d$ and its flat complement $T'=\bigoplus_{S_i\ne T}S_i$ in $W_{\mathbb C}$, using the chosen summand indices. Put $A=\bigwedge^dH_{\mathbb C}\otimes\bigwedge^{e-d}H_{\mathbb C}$ and $V=\bigwedge^dT\otimes\bigwedge^{e-d}T'\subset A$. The determinant identification for $W=T\oplus T'$ is flat, so step 1.1 makes $V^{\otimes2}\subset A^{\otimes2}$ a constant line. The rational object underlying $A^{\otimes2}$ is geometric by [F3]; its complex invariant part is the complexification of its rational invariant part, because invariants are common kernels of rational matrices, reducible to finitely many linear equations in a finite-dimensional fibre. By [F1] this fixed part is a constant Hodge structure. For any Hodge-torus element $t$, the image $t(V^{\otimes2})=(tV)^{\otimes2}$ is therefore a flat line in that fixed part. In a local flat frame choose a nonzero continuous generator $\sigma$ of $tV$; its squared projective class is constant. The map $[u]\mapsto[u\otimes u]$ is injective: if $u\otimes u$ and $v\otimes v$ are proportional, contraction with a functional nonzero on $u$ shows $v$ is proportional to $u$. Thus $[\sigma]$ is constant and $tV$ is flat. A decomposable tensor line in $E\otimes F$ determines its factor lines by contraction with $F^*$ and $E^*$; applying this to $tV$ shows that $\bigwedge^d(tT)$ is flat. Finally the Plücker line determines $tT$ by $tT=\{v:v\wedge p=0\}$ for any nonzero $p\in\bigwedge^d(tT)$, as is checked by completing a basis of $tT$ to a basis of the ambient space. This identity commutes with transport, so $tT$ is flat for every $t$. The case $e=d$ uses the constant zeroth exterior power and satisfies the same argument.

Openness of irreducibility and torus-stability of the socle. For $t$ near $1$ the flat subspace $tT$ is simple: were there $t_n\to1$ with $t_nT$ reducible, there would be, for each $n$, a proper nonzero flat subspace $U_n\subset t_nT$; their dimensions have finitely many possible values $\varrho$, $1\le\varrho<d$; pass to a subsequence with fixed $\varrho$, then use [F5] to make the orthogonal projections $P_n$ onto $U_n$ converge to a rank-$\varrho$ projection $P$. The inclusions $U_n\subset t_nT$ give $\operatorname{im}P\subset T$. For each monodromy matrix $M$, invariance is the closed matrix equation $(I-P_n)MP_n=0$; taking limits gives $(I-P)MP=0$ for every $M$. No finite generation of the fundamental group is assumed. Thus $U=\operatorname{im}P$ is a nonzero proper flat subspace of $T$, contradicting simplicity of $T$. Hence, for $t$ in a neighbourhood of $1$, each $tS_i$ is a simple flat subspace of $H_{\mathbb C}$, and every simple flat subspace is contained in the socle $W_{\mathbb C}$ by [F2]; summing over the finitely many $S_i$ gives $tW\subseteq W$, hence $tW=W$ by dimension. Thus the stabilizer of $W$ in $\mathbb C^\times$ contains a neighbourhood of the identity; a subgroup of a topological group with nonempty interior is open, and the connected group $\mathbb C^\times$ has no proper nonempty open subgroup, so $tW=W$ for every $t\in\mathbb C^\times$. Consequently $W_s$ is stable under the Hodge torus at every point $s$, so $W_{\mathbb Q}$ is a Hodge substructure of $H$ at every point; since it is already flat, it is a Hodge subvariation.

Polarization splitting and induction. Let $Q$ be a polarization of the pure object $H$. Its restriction to the Hodge subvariation $W$ is nondegenerate: if $v\in W_{s,\mathbb C}$ were a nonzero radical vector, then with the Weil operator $C$ of the Hodge structure the vector $C\bar v$ lies in $W_{s,\mathbb C}$ because $W_s$ is a Hodge substructure, so the positivity of the Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(v,v)=Q(Cv,\bar v)=(-1)^nQ(v,C\bar v)$ would give the contradiction $0=Q(v,C\bar v)\ne0$. Hence the $Q$-orthogonal complement $W^\perp$ is a flat Hodge subvariation and $H=W\oplus W^\perp$; the orthogonal projection onto $W$ is a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism, so $W^\perp$ is a geometric direct summand of $H$ by [F3], of smaller rank unless $W=H$. The submodule $W_{\mathbb C}$ is a direct sum of simples by construction, and by induction over the rank the complex monodromy module of $W^\perp$ is semisimple; a direct sum of semisimple modules is semisimple, so the complex monodromy module of $H$ is semisimple. A non-pure object is a finite direct sum of pure weight pieces, handled one weight at a time, and the rank-zero case is the empty direct sum.

Coefficient fields and the Gauss-Manin case. Complex semisimplicity of the monodromy module of $H$ means exactly that the complex local system $H\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple in the sense of [F4]. derivations.claim: (a) Define a $k$-algebra $E$ with $k$-basis $\{x_1^ax_2^be(ij),x_1^ax_2^be(ji),x_1^ax_2^b\tau e(ij),x_1^ax_2^b\tau e(ji)\}_{a,b\ge0}$ and multiplication determined by: $x_1,x_2$ commuting with each other and with the idempotents; $\tau e(ij)=e(ji)\tau$, $\tau e(ji)=e(ij)\tau$; $\tau^2=0$; and moving a dot across a crossing permutes the two variables. Associativity holds because the dot permutation is an algebra automorphism of $k[x_1,x_2]$, the idempotents are orthogonal, and every product containing two consecutive crossings or an idempotent mismatch is zero. The presentation of $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$ with $Q=0$ is satisfied by this model, so the universal property gives a surjection $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)\twoheadrightarrow E$, while the same Coxeter/dot reduction that proves spanning [F2] shows the model basis spans $R(\alpha_i+\alpha_j)$; a linear dependence among those spanning elements in $R$ would map to a dependence among basis elements of $E$, hence they are independent and the PBW basis of the statement holds for $Q=0$. This proves (a) without applying the nondegenerate PBW theorem outside its hypotheses.

(b) A product $P_{ij}(u,v)P_{ji}(v,u)=0$ in the domain $k[u,v]$ forces one factor to be zero, so no factorization has both factors nonzero; taking $P_{ij}=0$, $P_{ji}=1$ and applying the formula of [[thm-polynomial-representation-of-a-klr-algebra]] defines a legitimate action: on the $ij$ summand the crossing operator vanishes, on the $ji$ summand it is the swap. It kills the element $\tau_1e(ij)$, which is nonzero by the basis of step 1.1, so this action (and by the same argument every factorized action, since at least one corner factor vanishes) is not faithful; this is exactly the failure of the faithfulness hypothesis [F3].

(c) For the non-hermitian pair, associativity of the word $\tau_1\tau_1\tau_1$ on $e(ij)$ computed in the two groupings gives, using relation (4) on the $ij$ corner for the right grouping and on the $ji$ corner after passing through $\tau_1$ for the left grouping, $\bigl(Q_{ij}(x_2,x_1)-Q_{ji}(x_1,x_2)\bigr)\tau_1e(ij)=0$; the dot slides for distinct colours are used to move dots across the crossings in the outer factors. Substituting $Q_{ij}(u,v)=u+2v$ and $Q_{ji}(u,v)=u+v$ gives $(x_2+2x_1)-(x_1+x_2)=x_1$, so $x_1\tau_1e(ij)=0$; applying the dot slide $\tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1$ on the $ij$ corner gives $\tau_1x_2e(ij)=x_1\tau_1e(ij)=0$. The element $x_1\tau_1e(ij)$ belongs to the spanning family $\{x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1^\varepsilon e(\nu)\}$ and is nonzero in the free algebra of the presentation, so that spanning family is not linearly independent and the graded PBW claim fails; equivalently, Rouquier’s PBW criterion shows that PBW is equivalent to the hermitian symmetry $Q_{ij}(u,v)=Q_{ji}(v,u)$, which the pair violates, and the failure is a linear dependence rather than a degree mismatch.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix $i\in I$.
(a) In weight $\alpha_i$ there is one sequence, and $R(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]e(i)$: the only relations are that $x_1$ is central, so $\{x_1^a\}_{a\ge0}$ is a $k$-basis, $\deg x_1=2d_i$, and $\mathrm{gdim}\,R(\alpha_i)=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$. The algebra is commutative; up to shift its unique graded simple module is $k$ with $x_1$ acting by $0$, $R(\alpha_i)$ is the projective cover of that simple, and $[R(\alpha_i)]=[P_{i,1}]$ with $([P_{i,1}],[P_{i,1}])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}$.
(b) In weight $2\alpha_i$ one has $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$, the nil Hecke algebra of rank $2$, with $k$-basis $\{x_1^ax_2^b,\ x_1^ax_2^b\tau_1\}_{a,b\ge0}$, free of rank $2$ over $k[x_1,x_2]$, and relations (in the normalization of relation (6) of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]])
$$\tau_1^2=0,\qquad \tau_1x_1=x_2\tau_1+e(ii),\qquad \tau_1x_2=x_1\tau_1-e(ii).$$
Its graded dimension is $\dfrac{1+q^{-2d_i}}{(1-q^{2d_i})^2}$, and the element $e_{i,2}=x_1\tau_1$ is a nonzero idempotent of degree $0$ with $P_{i,2}=R(2\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,2})\{-d_i\}$ an indecomposable projective of class $[P_{i,2}]=\gamma(\theta_i^{(2)})$ in $K_0(R)$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finitely generated graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finitely generated graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

u B_K$ on the weight component $
u$, $C_
u=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-
u_i}$, the Lusztig-normalized form of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]]. Then for homogeneous $x,y\in Af_
u$ the Cartan pairing of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] satisfies
$$(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))_{KLR}=B_L(x,y)=C_
u\,B_K(x,y),$$
where $\gamma:Af	o K_0(R)$ is the algebra homomorphism of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]. Equivalently, the two bilinear forms are equal under the identification of divided-power classes; in particular the KLR pairing is $\mathbb Q(q)$-nondegenerate on each finite weight component $Af_
u\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)$ after extending scalars, and $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))'_{KLR}=B_L(\overline{x},y)$, where bar acts on the first input. On generators: $([P_i],[P_j])=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}=B_L(	heta_i,	heta_j)$ and $([P_{i,n}],[P_{i,n}])=B_L(	heta_i^{(n)},	heta_i^{(n)})=\prod_{a=1}^n(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Fix a graded $k$-algebra $A$ and let $P$ be a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). The category
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ of graded left $A$-modules and degree-zero maps is
abelian ([[lem-graded-module-kernels-cokernels-and-biproducts-are-degreewise]]).

**Graded projective.** $P$ is **graded projective** when it is a projective
object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ ([[def-projective-object]]): for every
degree-zero epimorphism $q:E\twoheadrightarrow M$ and every degree-zero
$f:P\to M$ there exists a degree-zero $\widetilde f:P\to E$ with
$q\widetilde f=f$. Thus projectivity is tested only against degree-zero
epimorphisms and degree-zero maps, and the lift need not be unique.

**Finitely generated.** $P$ is **finitely generated as a graded left
$A$-module**, or generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, when for some
$n\ge0$ there are homogeneous elements $p_1,\dots,p_n\in P$ with

$$P=A p_1+\cdots+A p_n .$$

By [[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]] this is the same
notion as finite generation of the underlying $A$-module: a finite homogeneous
family is a finite family, and conversely, if $P=\langle S\rangle_A$ for a
finite set $S$, then writing each $s=\sum_es_e$ as its finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components gives, for every $x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s s\in P$,

$$x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s\sum_es_e=\sum_{s,e}a_s s_e,$$

a finite $A$-linear combination of the homogeneous elements $s_e\in P$; so the
finitely many components of the members of $S$ generate $P$. In particular the
notion does not depend on the chosen finite generating set.

**Finite graded projective.** $P$ is **finite graded projective** when it is
graded projective and generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, that is,
when it is graded projective and finitely generated as an $A$-module. The family
may be empty: $n=0$ gives $P=Ap_1+\cdots+Ap_n=0$, so the zero module is
generated by the empty homogeneous family, and the corresponding finite direct
sum of shifts in the characterization below is the empty direct sum. Its finite
shifted-free characterization is the next result
([[thm-finite-graded-projectives-are-summands-of-finite-graded-free-modules]]),
and it uses this same notion of finite generation throughout: a finite
homogeneous generating family there is exactly a family as above. No choice
principle is used in the equivalence above, which only rewrites a given finite
expression.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra. A **graded-simple module** here means a
nonzero finite-dimensional graded left $A$-module whose only graded submodules
are $0$ and itself. Internal shift acts on graded-simple isomorphism classes
by $[S]\mapsto[S\{r\}]$ for $r\in\mathbb Z$. There are finitely many shift
orbits of graded-simple isomorphism classes. For each orbit choose a
representative $S_i$ and a finite graded projective cover
$p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$, whose kernel is superfluous among graded

$$

derivations.claim: (Central polynomial subalgebra and freeness.) Let $C_\beta$ be the color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra: on the summand $e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\nu)$ it is the polynomial ring in the elementary symmetric functions of the dots of each color separately. It is central: unequal crossings permute dot positions, and equal-color divided differences $\partial_a$ commute with symmetric polynomials in $x_a,x_{a+1}$ by the Leibniz rule $\partial_a(fg)=\partial_a(f)g+s_a(f)\partial_a(g)$ applied to $s_a$-invariant $f$. In each constant-color block of length $m$ the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ is free over the symmetric subring on the Artin monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_m^{a_m}$, $0\le a_r\le m-r$: adjoining the first root of the universal polynomial $T^m-e_1T^{m-1}+\cdots+(-1)^me_m$ presents $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ as a free rank-$m$ module over the coefficient ring, the corresponding quotient of $T^m-\cdots$ by $T-x_1$ is monic of degree $m-1$ with the correct coefficients, and iteration gives those monomials as a basis while the elementary symmetric functions of the roots recover the $e_r$. Combining with the PBW basis [F1], whose dot monomials factor over the color blocks, gives that $R(\beta)$ is a finite free $C_\beta$-module, of rank $(|\beta|!)^2$ per weight counting the permutation basis; only centrality and this freeness are used below.

(Krull-Schmidt and splitting.) Every finitely generated graded module is bounded below and locally finite by [F1]. Choose finitely many homogeneous generators of degrees $d_j$; evaluation on the generators injects $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ into the finite product of the finitely many finite-dimensional pieces $M_{d_j}$, so every degree-zero endomorphism algebra is finite-dimensional, and a nontrivial homogeneous idempotent splits $M$ into two nonzero summands with strictly smaller endomorphism algebras; splitting terminates. For an indecomposable $M$, every endomorphism $f$ satisfies a polynomial minimal equation because $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ is finite-dimensional; factoring it as $T^rg(T)$ with $g(0)\ne0$, Bezout gives a polynomial projector separating the nilpotent part from the invertible part, so indecomposability forces $f$ or $1-f$ to be invertible. Hence the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal, and the usual comparison of two decompositions $\bigoplus p_ii_jp_j=\mathrm{id}$ produces a matching summand and cancellation, proving uniqueness in the degree-zero category; the shifts are recorded as part of each summand.

(Simples and covers.) For a graded simple $S$ and a positive-degree central $c\in C_\beta^+$, the kernel and image of $c$ are graded submodules; if $c$ acted nontrivially it would be injective and hence surjective, contradicting the least nonzero degree of the bounded-below module $S$; so $C_\beta^+S=0$ and $S$ is finite-dimensional because $\bar R=R(\beta)/C_\beta^+R(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional by step 1.1. The finite-dimensional basis theorem [F3] applies to $\bar R$: it has finitely many graded simple shift orbits, and the same then holds for $R(\beta)$, since any simple $R(\beta)$-module is one. Projective covers are then lifted to $R(\beta)$: choose a finite shifted-free $R$-module $F$ whose reduction $\bar F$ surjects onto the projective cover $\bar Q\twoheadrightarrow\bar S$. That surjection splits by projectivity of $\bar Q$, giving an idempotent of $\operatorname{End}^0_{\bar R}(\bar F)$; entrywise reduction $\operatorname{End}^0_R(F)\to\operatorname{End}^0_{\bar R}(\bar F)$ is surjective; the reduction kernel in $\operatorname{End}^0_R(F)$ is nilpotent because its entries have positive central degree and a long product has degree exceeding every fixed difference of generator degrees minus the lower bound of $F$, so the projector onto $\bar Q$ is lifted by the finite nilpotent-ideal idempotent-lifting iteration $e\mapsto e-(2e-1)(e^2-e)$; the image $Q$ of the lifted projector is projective, its kernel is graded superfluous (after reduction by $C^+$ it is superfluous for $\bar Q$, and a bounded-below graded quotient $X=C^+X$ vanishes by its least nonzero degree), so $Q$ is an indecomposable projective cover, and every indecomposable projective is such a cover up to shift.

(Orbit bases.) Finite decompositions into indecomposables give that $K_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of indecomposable finite graded projectives, with $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$, and finite length of finite-dimensional modules gives that $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the simple shift orbits; both are $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-modules in the sense of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], the shift action is free because a nonzero finite-dimensional graded module is not isomorphic to a nonzero shift of itself (compare its least and greatest degrees), and the finite-dimensional theorem [F3] gives the same statement for the quotient categories. For a projective cover $P_b$ and simple $S_c$ with their selected shifts, $\operatorname{Hom}(P_b,S_c)=0$ unless $b=c$ at the selected shift, when it equals $\operatorname{End}(S_b)$ by the uniqueness of the cover, whose degree-zero endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra by Schur's argument; finite-dimensionality alone does not identify it with $k$; this is the diagonal-entry computation of the Hom pairing of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]. The stronger statement that the diagonal scalar rings equal $k$ over every field, and the associated unscaled dual-basis conclusion, are not inferred here from finite-dimensional algebra alone and are proved separately later on this page; nothing above uses them.

The End^0 reduction kernel is nilpotent by increasing central degree versus bounded generator-degree differences, allowing the stated idempotent lift and graded-superfluous-kernel cover. Cover heads exclude nonzero projective shift periodicity; simple endomorphism rings are not prematurely identified with k. beta=0 reduces to finite-dimensional graded k-vector spaces. citations.quote: Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $Af$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free $A$-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free $A$-rank of $Af_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finitely generated graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finitely generated graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $Af$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i'$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$\varepsilon\colon U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the **augmentation**, the projection
onto the degree-zero component $U_q^-[0]=\mathbb Q(q)\cdot1$ (so
$\varepsilon(Q)=0$ on all positive-height components and $\varepsilon(1)=1$).

The **normalized Lusztig–Kashiwara form** on $U_q^-$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon U_q^-\times U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(H) $B$ is **homogeneous**: $B\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu]\bigr)=0$ whenever
$\nu\ne\mu$;

(N) $B(1,1)=1$;

(R) $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ for all $i\in I$ and all $P,Q\in U_q^-$.

Equivalently, axioms (H) and (N) may be replaced by the single **counit
normalization**

(C) $B(1,Q)=\varepsilon(Q)$ for all $Q\in U_q^-$,

in the presence of (R) (Verification, step 1.1).

Axioms (H) and (N) (equivalently (C)) are essential and not redundant: the
recursion (R) together with $B(1,1)=1$ alone neither forces symmetry nor
uniqueness, as the rank-one witness of step 2.2 shows.

The axioms determine $B$ uniquely: peeling first letters in the first argument
writes every positive-height $P$ as a finite sum $P=\sum_iF_iP_i$ and evaluates
$B(P,Q)=\sum_iB(P_i,e_i'Q)$, reducing the height; the base of the induction is
(C) (Verification, step 2.1). The **existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy** of
$B$ on $U_q^-$ for the actual quotient by the Serre ideal are not proved here:
they are the content of the negative-half form theorem
`thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral`,
the declared justification of this definition, which also settles the exact
integrality normalization ($A$-valuedness on the word lattice and the
Gaussian-factorial denominators on the divided-power lattice). That theorem
is proved on this page, and its statement is the declared supplier of
existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy; this definition itself claims only that
(H), (N) and (R) determine $B$ and that the normalization cannot be relaxed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation over $\mathbb Q(v)$, where $v$ is an indeterminate and $v_i=v^{d_i}$; the transport below sends $v_i$ to $q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. > ([[def-choice-function]]).

$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$

$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. $$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).

Let $A$ and $B$ be graded $k$-algebras and $M$ a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule. Write
$\Phi_M:=M\otimes_A-$ for the functor that sends a graded left $A$-module $N$ to
the graded left $B$-module $M\otimes_AN$ of the total-degree grading.

1. **Exactness.** If $M$ is flat as an underlying right $A$-module, then
$\Phi_M$ is exact on graded left $A$-modules.

2. **Projectives.** If $M$ is finite graded projective as a left $B$-module,
then $\Phi_M$ carries every finite graded projective left $A$-module to a finite
graded projective left $B$-module.

Neither hypothesis is asserted to imply the other; the companion page exhibits
a right-flat $M$ whose output is not projective and a left-projective $M$ whose
tensor functor is not exact.

Let $A$ and $B$ be graded $k$-algebras, let $M$ be a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule, $X$
a graded left $A$-module and $Y$ a graded left $B$-module. Then currying

$$\Theta:\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(M\otimes_AX,Y)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}\bigl(X,\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)\bigr),\qquad \Theta(F)(x)(m):=F(m\otimes x),$$

is a natural bijection in $X$ and $Y$, where
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is the graded left $A$-module of finite sums of
homogeneous $B$-linear maps with the associative action
$(a\cdot f)(m)=f(ma)$. Its inverse sends $f$ to the map $m\otimes x\mapsto
f(x)(m)$ on elementary tensors.

Separately, the same formulas give a natural bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M\otimes_AX,Y)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(X,\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M,Y))$
between ungraded module maps. Here $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is the direct sum
of its homogeneous parts and can be properly contained in
$\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M,Y)$, so the graded statement cannot be
replaced by one with all ungraded maps on the right.

**Total internal degree on the balanced tensor product.** Let $A$ be a graded
$k$-algebra, $M$ a graded right $A$-module and $N$ a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). First use the canonical
decomposition of the ordinary tensor product of the underlying abelian groups
$$M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N\cong\bigoplus_{i,j\in\mathbb Z}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j.$$
Its inverse sends $m\otimes n$ to the finite sum
$\sum_{i,j}m_i\otimes n_j$, where $m=\sum_i m_i$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are their
homogeneous decompositions; the two maps are inverse because they agree with
the identity on homogeneous elementary tensors. Give the summand
$M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$ total degree $i+j$, and write
$G_d:=\bigoplus_{i+j=d}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$.

The balanced tensor product
$M\otimes_AN=(M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N)/\mathcal R_A$
([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), where
$\mathcal R_A$ is generated by the balance relations
$(ma)\otimes n-m\otimes(an)$. These relations are generated by the homogeneous
ones: for $m=\sum_i m_i$, $a=\sum_\ell a_\ell$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$, the relation
is the finite sum of
$(m_i a_\ell)\otimes n_j-m_i\otimes(a_\ell n_j)$ over $i,\ell,j$. Each such
homogeneous relation belongs to $G_{i+\ell+j}$, since the two module actions
preserve total degree. Thus $\mathcal R_A=\bigoplus_d(\mathcal R_A\cap G_d)$,
and

$$M\otimes_AN=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(M\otimes_AN)_d,\qquad (M\otimes_AN)_d:=(G_d+\mathcal R_A)/\mathcal R_A,$$

is a graded abelian group. For homogeneous $m\in M_i$ and $n\in N_j$ the
elementary tensor $m\otimes n$ has **total internal degree** $i+j$; every tensor
is a finite sum of homogeneous elementary tensors, and the balancing relations
used in the quotient are homogeneous. This grading is the only grading used
below, and it introduces no sign.

**Outer actions.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $N$ a graded left
$A$-module, then the action $b(m\otimes n):=(bm)\otimes n$ of
[[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]] makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded
left $B$-module: the action is homogeneous because homogeneous $b\in B_l$ sends
$m\otimes n$ of degree $i+j$ to an element of degree $l+i+j$. Symmetrically, if
$N$ is a graded $(A,C)$-bimodule, the action
$(m\otimes n)c:=m\otimes(nc)$ makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded right $C$-module, and
the two outer actions commute when both are present.

**Homogeneous Hom.** For graded left $A$-modules $P,Q$, with
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$ the abelian group of all $A$-linear
maps $P\to Q$, put

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q):=\bigl\{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)\mid f(P_i)\subseteq Q_{i+d}\ \text{for all }i\in\mathbb Z\bigr\},\qquad \operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q):=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q).$$

Each $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$ is a subgroup of
$\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$, and the sum is direct: if
$f=\sum_df_d=\sum_df'_d$ with $f_d,f'_d\in\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}$, then for
$p\in P_i$ the element $f(p)$ has homogeneous components
$f_d(p)\in Q_{i+d}$, and comparison of the graded components in $Q$ gives
$f_d(p)=f'_d(p)$ for every $d$ and $p$, so $f_d=f'_d$. Thus
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$ is a graded abelian group whose degree-$d$ part is
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$, and the degree-zero morphisms are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(P,Q)$. By definition $\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$
consists of the finite sums of homogeneous $A$-linear maps, so
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(P,Q)$
with equality only when every $A$-linear map has bounded spread in degree.

**The associative left action.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $Y$ a
graded left $B$-module, then $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ carries a left
$A$-module structure

$$(a\cdot f)(m):=f(ma)\qquad(a\in A,\ m\in M),$$

which is homogeneous: for $a\in A_i$ and $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d}(M,Y)$ one
has $ma\in M_{l+i}$ for $m\in M_l$, hence $(a\cdot f)(m)\in Y_{l+i+d}$ and
$a\cdot f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{B,d+i}(M,Y)$. The action is associative and
unital by the module axioms of $M$, so $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is a graded
left $A$-module and an object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$. The same formula
defines an action on the full ungraded $\operatorname{Hom}$ group, where it is
denoted by the same symbol.

derivations.claim: (Shuffle decomposition and freeness.) Choose reduced PBW words adapted to the parabolic subgroup $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$. For each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ and minimal right coset representative $w$, the vectors $\tau_we(\xi)b$, with $b$ ranging through the PBW basis of $e(\xi)B$, form precisely the PBW basis of the right $B$-module $Ae$: the permutation is a minimal shuffle followed by an internal block permutation, with additive length, and the right idempotent records the source word in the corner $e$. Thus $Ae\cong\bigoplus_{w,\xi}e(\xi)B\{\delta_R(w,\xi)\}$, with the displayed degree of $\tau_we(\xi)$. Reversal of products fixing dots, crossings and idempotents preserves the defining relations and is an anti-involution; it sends $Ae$ to $eA$ and $\tau_we(\xi)$ to $e(\xi)\tau_{w^{-1}}$, giving the left $B$-module decomposition of $eA$ into the corresponding $Be(\xi)$ with shifts $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)$. Both decompositions are finite sums of principal graded projectives. Ungraded, for each shuffle the sum over all concatenated $\xi$ is one copy of $B$, so both ranks are $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. Neither bimodule is replaced by $eAe$: its unconstrained opposite endpoint is essential for the shuffle basis.

(Left adjunction.) For a graded left $B$-module $X$ and a graded left $A$-module $L$, currying gives the natural degree-zero bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(Ae\otimes_BX,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(X,eL)$, $\Phi\mapsto(x\mapsto\Phi(e\otimes x))$, with inverse $f\mapsto(ae\otimes x\mapsto a\,f(x))$, well defined on balanced tensors and inverse by the idempotence of $e$; this is the adjunction of [F3] for the $(A,B)$-bimodule $Ae$.

(Exactness and projectivity.) The right $B$-module $Ae$ is projective, hence flat, by step 1.1, so $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ is exact by [F2]. Idempotent restriction is exact on left modules: for a surjection $L\to N$, a vector $en\in eN$ lifts to $e\ell\in eL$, and kernels and images commute with multiplication by the degree-zero idempotent $e$; no right action on $L$ is required. A finitely generated graded projective left $B$-module is a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $B$, so its induction is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $Ae$. As a left $A$-module $Ae$ is the image of the degree-zero idempotent endomorphism $a\mapsto ae$ of $A$, hence is finitely generated graded projective. Similarly, if $P$ is a finitely generated graded projective left $A$-module, realize $P$ as a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $A$ and apply $e(-)$ to its split inclusion and projection. Then $eP$ is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $eA$, which is finitely generated graded projective as a left $B$-module by step 1.1. Internal shifts commute with induction and restriction because their balance relations and idempotent action have degree zero. This proves exactness, shift compatibility and both finite-projective preservation clauses.

(Coinduction and the longest shuffle.) The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$ by [F3] applied to $M=eA$, and explicit currying gives $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$. For the second-adjunction formula let $y$ be the longest block shuffle of the two blocks, of degree $-c$ (each of the $|\beta||\gamma|$ crossed positions contributes the negative pairing of the two colours), and let $e'=e(\gamma,\beta)$ be the reversed-block idempotent. By PBW there is a well-defined $B$-balanced coefficient map $t:eAe'\to B$ projecting onto the $y$-coefficient, where the reversed block order is read in $B$ through the flip equivalence $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)\to R(\gamma)\otimes_kR(\beta)$; dot slides and block crossings preserve the longest-shuffle coefficient, while every dot or braid correction in a shorter shuffle has strictly smaller shuffle length and is killed by $t$. Hence the map $\Phi:Ae'\to\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)$, $z\mapsto(u\mapsto t(uz))$, is a degree-$c$ map of $(A,B)$-bimodules, and it is compatible with the flip identification.

(Mackey filtration.) Fix a second flag with idempotent $e'=e(\beta',\gamma')$ and choose reduced double-coset representatives for the row block permutation group and the column block permutation group acting on the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ positions. Partition the PBW monomials of the corner $eAe'$ by the four intersection blocks $(a,b;c,d)$ with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, and filter by the crossing length of the double-coset representatives. The span of the double cosets of strictly smaller length is a $(B,B')$-sub-bimodule: sliding a block generator across a representative either stays in its double coset with an internal block permutation, or produces a quadratic/braid correction of strictly smaller length, which lies in the smaller span. In the associated quotient only the monomials whose permutation is the minimal double-coset representative survive; they are exactly tensor products of the PBW bases of the four blocks composed with the row and column induced bimodules and the unique minimal crossing of the two middle blocks, which carries the shift $-(b\mid c)$ because the crossed colours are precisely $b$ and $c$. The basis bijection defines inverse maps between the associated quotient and the composite four-block restriction/induction bimodule, so the filtration is proved and not merely a character identity; iterating the same permutation argument gives the multi-block statement.

(Triangularity and the functor formula.) Pair the right $B$-module shuffle basis of $Ae'$ (through the block flip) with the left $B$-module shuffle basis of $eA$ by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, the coefficient matrix of the pairing $u\mapsto t(uz)$ is triangular: a complementary pair is exactly the reduced longest shuffle with coefficient $1$ up to the absorbed equal-colour signs, and a noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic or braid correction to strictly smaller length, hence vanishes in the associated graded. Finite triangular elimination over $B$ (division by the diagonal units $1$) inverts the matrix, so $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of graded $(A,B)$-bimodules; consequently $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\cong Ae'\{c\}$ with the $B$-action transported by the block flip. Since $eA$ is finite projective over $B$ by step 1.1, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\otimes_BX\cong\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,X)$ for every graded $B$-module $X$ (checked on finite free modules and finite summands), and tracking the outer right $B$-action through the flip gives the functorial isomorphism $\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}$.

All clauses of the statement are now proved: step 1.1 gives the freeness and the labelled shuffle shifts, step 2.1 the exactness, shift compatibility and projective preservation, step 1.2 the left adjunction, steps 2.2 and 3.1 the right adjoint and its exact reversed-block formula, and step 2.3 the finite Mackey filtration and its multi-block version.

1. **Braid moves.** Call two words in $S$ *braid-equivalent* when one is obtained from the other by finitely many replacements of an alternating subword $s\,t\,s\,t\cdots$ of length $m(s,t)<\infty$ by the alternating word $t\,s\,t\,s\cdots$ of the same length. Then any two reduced expressions of the same element $w\in W$ are braid-equivalent.
2. **M-reducedness.** A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it (M-reduced in the sense of [Davis, Definition 3.4.1]).
3. **Singleton detection in dihedral subgroups.** Fix distinct $s,t\in S$ and put $m:=m(s,t)$. The subgroup $\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ is dihedral of order $2m$ when $m<\infty$ and infinite dihedral when $m=\infty$; every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ acts on the quotient $E/\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ as the identity, while for every $u\in S\setminus\{s,t\}$ one has $\sigma_u(\alpha_u)-\alpha_u=-2\alpha_u\notin\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ (no induced quotient map for $\sigma_u$ is assumed). Consequently
$$S\cap\langle s,t\rangle=\{s,t\},$$
and every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ has a reduced expression with all letters in $\{s,t\}$ (so the alternating words of length $q\le m$, and any $q$ when $m=\infty$, are reduced in $W$).

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. Put $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$, $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$ and $c=(\beta\mid\gamma)$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix; let $W$ and $\ell$ be the presented group and its length and let $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ be the geometric representation, as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], with reflection set $T$ and sign-change sets $\Phi(w)$ as in that lemma. Parts (1) and (2) hold for every finite $S$, including the empty and singleton cases; a distinct pair is required only for part (3).

1. **Braid moves.** Call two words in $S$ *braid-equivalent* when one is obtained from the other by finitely many replacements of an alternating subword $s\,t\,s\,t\cdots$ of length $m(s,t)<\infty$ by the alternating word $t\,s\,t\,s\cdots$ of the same length. Then any two reduced expressions of the same element $w\in W$ are braid-equivalent.
2. **M-reducedness.** A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it (M-reduced in the sense of [Davis, Definition 3.4.1]).
3. **Singleton detection in dihedral subgroups.** Fix distinct $s,t\in S$ and put $m:=m(s,t)$. The subgroup $\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ is dihedral of order $2m$ when $m<\infty$ and infinite dihedral when $m=\infty$; every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ acts on the quotient $E/\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ as the identity, while for every $u\in S\setminus\{s,t\}$ one has $\sigma_u(\alpha_u)-\alpha_u=-2\alpha_u\notin\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ (no induced quotient map for $\sigma_u$ is assumed). Consequently
$$S\cap\langle s,t\rangle=\{s,t\},$$
and every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ has a reduced expression with all letters in $\{s,t\}$ (so the alternating words of length $q\le m$, and any $q$ when $m=\infty$, are reduced in $W$).

Then the homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $Af$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free $A$-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free $A$-rank of $Af_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail.
